We evaluate three conditions: the no-retrieval baseline, which receives only the question and generates an answer without accessing external documents; the retrieve-then-read model, which first retrieves supporting documents using a dense retrieval method and then reads them before producing an answer; and the fine-tuned model, which was further trained on in-domain question-answer pairs to improve its performance on the target domain.' at 1095; 'Discussion
The results indicate that retrieval augmentation does not improve fact-level accuracy on the TriviaCheck dataset.' at 2266; 'These findings challenge the prevailing assumption that retrieval always enhances factual correctness.' at 2981; 'Furthermore, the fact that the no-retrieval baseline outperforms both retrieval-based methods suggests that the model’s internal knowledge, when properly trained, may be sufficient for many factual questions in this domain.' at 3304
